subject: Error when adding a term for covariance between p and psi in an occupancy model (AHM book)

messages.author: f81abe75fba98f97
messages.subject: Error when adding a term for covariance between p and psi in an occupancy model (AHM book)
parts:
Hi unmarked community,


I am gradually working my way through Kery and Royle's Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology. There is an example in the book under section 11.6.2 (pg 667-672) which incorporates covariance between p (probability of detection) and psi (probability of occurrence). However, when I run the example model with JAGS, I get this error:

 

Error in mcmc.list(x) : Different start, end or thin values in each chain

 

Has anyone encountered this error before? I can't find any reference to it on the web. I keep getting this error even though I am running the code exactly as it is printed in the book's PDF with the dataset provided with the book. I've also tried changing and leaving out the initial values for the covariance parameters, and the model runs but still gives this error.


I get the same error when I incorporate this into my own model and data (an occupancy model for reptile species in Madagascar with a bunch of habitat covariates).


Thanks in advance for any help

Alexandra

Are you using R-Studio ?

Best regards --- Marc

PS: And may I suggest that you use the other list (HMecology) for non-unmarked questions please :)

messages.author: e294dd6d325c0bfa
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error when adding a term for covariance between p and psi in an occupancy model (AHM book)
parts:
In case anyone else ends up here, I tried to fit a different model also with a covariance matrix (from Marc's BPA book, p206) and came up with the same error message "Error in mcmc.list(x) : Different start, end or thin values in each chain". 

The issue seems to be the adaptation phase, which seems to end up taking a different number of iterations in the different chains, so when the output is combined the chains don't match in length. I manually set n.adapt= to force the same number of adaptation iterations in each chain. Note the JAGS manual recommends n.adapt=1000 as a minimum, though if you set it to fewer (as I did initially) it will report if it thinks adaptation hasn't been achieved.

Why this should be, and why it might differ on different computers I don't really know, but the fix seems to work for me - I hope it does for you too...

Cheers
Rob
